messages:
maria: quick brain-dump — we need a tight eval protocol for running speculative decoding on quantized variants (Q4/INT4) before we push any fallbacks to Dedicated. main concerns: quality regressions on rare tokens, safety drift, and tail-latency savings that actually translate to cost.
akash: how big an eval set are you thinking? random web prompts won't cut it for rare-token regressions.
jun: propose: stratified eval of 10k prompts: 6k high-frequency/LLM-friendly, 3k long-context (>=1024 tokens), 1k rare-token / factual-check subset. paired A/B (same seeds) between baseline non-spec and spec pipeline. measure: exact-match/EM (where applicable), BLEU/ROUGE for longform, perplexity delta, and a hallucination score (model-asserted fact vs external KB matcher).
ben: +1. also capture anchored human checks on 500 examples sampled from the failures (100 each strat). we should compute paired bootstrap p-values for metric deltas. target detection threshold: p<0.05 and effect-size > 0.5% for perf metrics, >0.2% for safety metrics (we're conservative).
rachel: human eval plan: hire from existing vendor. label schema: correct/incorrect/partially-correct/hallucinated/toxic. do pairwise judgments to reduce annotator bias. provide clear instructions and 3 gold checks per worker.
maria: operational notes: fallback policy should be deterministic for canary (i.e., if spec-confidence < 0.9 then sync fallback). we need telemetry: per-token spec-hits, average speculative window size, KV-cache churn. If spec-hit lowers log-prob mass on top-1 by >5% on rare-token set, fail canary.
jun: ran a quick smoke on titan-q4 (toy): 1k stratified prompts. results w/ speculative factor=2, predictor-temp=0.8:

```
latency (p50/p95): baseline 180ms / 420ms -> spec 120ms / 310ms  (p95 -26%)
throughput (+20% tokens/sec)
EM delta (factual subset): -0.8% (p=0.12)
hallucination rate: +0.4% (p=0.04)
self-perplexity shift: +1.6% on rare-token bin
spec-hit rate: 72%
```
jun: early signal: latency wins are real, but small safety drift on hallucination is statistically detectable. need larger N and human checks.
ben: question — are we measuring after quantization-aware calibration? QAT tends to change softmax sharpness; spec predictor might become overconfident.
maria: good catch. plan: test three axes independently: (A) full-precision spec, (B) quantized spec w/o QAT calibrations, (C) quantized + QAT calibrations. then run canary pipeline: if (C) passes, promote.
akash: any recommended config snippet for the experiment? want to replicate quickly on Dedicated.
maria: yes — CLI + config we used (toy):

```
# run-speculative --model titan-q4 --spec-factor 2 --predictor-temp 0.8 \
  --fallback-threshold 0.9 --eval-set path://s3/experiments/spec-2026/stratified-10k.json \
  --log-metrics spec_hits,window_size,kv_churn,top1_mass,per-token-lp
```
maria: and example fallback policy JSON:

```
{
  "type": "confidence",
  "threshold": 0.9,
  "on_fail": "sync-fallback",
  "max_window": 8
}
```
rachel: for the human batch, give annotators both spec and baseline outputs side-by-side blind. ask for preference and mark hallucination. that'll speed analysis.
deploy-bot: canary created for eng-ml/speculative-q4-2026 — 50 requests/min for 2h window. link: https://console.redwood/spec-canary/12345
maria: thanks — next actions: jun expand to 10k, run 3-axis matrix, produce short report with paired stats + top-100 failure examples for human annotation. I'll draft rollout runbook for canary -> ramp -> rollback thresholds.
akash: flagging infra: make sure token-level tracing retention is 24h for the run so we can repro KV churn. otherwise we'll be blind.
jun: will kick off the 10k job now and post results here when done.
